overview.description: Bruus North Friesland is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from North Friesland in northern Germany. It uses a 36-card French-suited pack with wildly disturbed card rankings, daring and striking bonuses, and a race to a target score tracked with matchsticks.
overview.deck: 36 cards (French-suited A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit; 5-2 removed)

history.origins: Bruus is a north German card game originating in North Friesland and neighbouring Schleswig. It descends from the medieval Karnöffel family and has been played for over 300 years, reaching particular popularity around Hamburg before surviving in a few villages near Husum and Treia.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.
nullReasons.cultural: No specific cultural or regional significance documented beyond its origins.

engine.deckDescription: One 36-card French-suited pack consisting of clubs, spades, hearts, and diamonds, each with the ranks A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, and 6. The deck is typically made by removing the fives, fours, threes and twos from a standard 52-card pack, as described for Bruus on Pagat.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds). In Bruus there is no single trump suit; instead, special matadors and beaters in every suit outrank ordinary cards, and the suits themselves rank clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds as in Skat.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit in the 36-card pack: ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven and six. Certain ranks such as the J of clubs, K of hearts, 8 of spades, nines, aces, jacks and sixes form powerful matadors and beaters, while remaining kings, eights, queens and tens act as duds that cannot beat other cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: Bruus North Friesland is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

scoring.description: Partnerships score matchsticks for winning at least five of the nine tricks in a deal and for successful daring and striking of the matador cards, tracking a running total of points.
scoring.winCondition: The first partnership to reach at least 12 points (matchsticks) through tricks and daring/striking matadors wins the game.

nullReasons.targetScore: Target score is a race to 12 matchsticks; the first team to reach 12 or more points wins the game.
nullReasons.scoringDirection: Scoring direction is high_wins; higher cumulative matchstick totals decide the winning partnership.
nullReasons.cardValues: Bruus scores with tricks and matchstick points from daring and striking; there are no separate per-card pip values to enumerate.
